title: Search
goal: Move anywhere with search, use search as a motion, and change text across the file with :s.

lessons.title: Search: / ? n N

concepts.desc: next / previous match in the search direction.
jump back to where you were before the search.

lessons.tip: Search is the fastest long-distance motion. If you can see a unique word, /word<CR> gets you there.

quiz.q: Search forward for timeout?
Go to the next match?
After a ? search, which way does n go?
quiz.a: Backward (n follows the search direction; N goes the other way).

quiz.q: Clear the search highlighting?
Jump back to where you were before searching?
Search backward for ERROR?

lessons.title: * # cgn and search as a motion

concepts.desc: search forward / backward for the whole word under the cursor.
delete from the cursor up to the match (any operator works: c/, y/).
select the next match; cgn changes it.
change one match, then . changes the next one: a precise search-and-replace.

lessons.tip: *  +  cgn  +  . . . is a selective rename: press n to skip a match you want to keep.

quiz.q: Find the next occurrence of the word under the cursor?
Delete from the cursor up to the next occurrence of 'end'?
What does cgn do?
quiz.a: Changes the next search match (and is repeatable with .).

quiz.q: Find the previous occurrence of the word under the cursor?
After cgn, how do you skip one match and change the following one?
Difference between * and g*?
quiz.a: * matches the whole word only (\<word\>); g* also matches it inside longer words.

lessons.title: Substitute: :s and :%s

concepts.desc: replace the first match on the current line.
replace all matches on the line.
g = all per line, c = confirm each, i / I = ignore / match case.

lessons.tip: Add c (:%s/a/b/gc) when you're not sure: y/n per match, a for all, q to quit.

quiz.q: Replace foo with bar everywhere in the file?
What does the c flag do?
quiz.a: Asks for confirmation at each match.

quiz.q: Replace only the first match on the current line?
Replace case-insensitively?
quiz.a: add the i flag: :%s/foo/bar/gi (or \c in the pattern)

quiz.q: What does the g flag mean?
quiz.a: Replace all matches on each line, not just the first.

quiz.q: Replace on line 10 only?

lessons.title: Ranges and patterns in :s

concepts.desc: in the replacement: the whole match (:s/\d\+/[&]/).
word char, digit, one or more, anything.
an empty pattern reuses the last search (search with * first).

lessons.tip: Build the pattern with / first and watch the highlights, then run :%s//replacement/g.

quiz.q: Replace on lines 5 to 10 only?
Match 'cat' but not 'category'?
What does & mean in the replacement?
Swap 'John Smith' to 'Smith, John'?
Replace from the current line to the end of the file?
What does :%s//X/g do?
quiz.a: Replaces matches of the last search pattern with X.

lessons.title: Week 4 review
lessons.tip: Pick the tool: one-off far away? /. Same word many times? * + cgn. Every match in a range? :s.

quiz.q: Rename a variable everywhere, whole words only?
Jump to the next occurrence of the word under the cursor?
Change from the cursor to the word 'end'?
Replace with confirmation in the whole file?
Wrap every number on lines 1-5 in brackets?
Go to the previous search match?
